rows.layout: Rows[tid][0..3] -> v4..v7 (first 32 of the 64 table rows: the wave32 run dispatches waveSize=32 threads)

notes: Wave32 run: one workgroup of 32 threads, LDS waveSize*32 = 1024 dwords (4096 B) = the oracle's group segment, so out-of-range behaviour matches. Bases are set in the body: v80 = lane*4, v81 = lane*8, v82 = lane*16 (words 5..7), sub-dword bases v83..v86 and v88..v91 derived from inputs. Highest addresses: ds_read_b32 v80 offset:4032 (up to byte 4159) and ds_read_b64 v81 offset:3968 (up to 4223) deliberately cross the 4 KiB end for the upper lanes; everything else stays below 4096. No rebasing possible (immediates) or wanted.

Words 8..136 fill all 32 planes (bytes 0..4095) with v4 + k*0x1000193 before any read, so uninitialised oracle LDS does not leak in-range; out-of-range reads return whatever the hardware returns for a 4 KiB allocation, which is what the test pins.
Two EXEC-masked sections (s_and_saveexec_b32 s20 on input >> 30 != 0) are restored by the body itself (words 207, 250: s_mov_b32 exec_lo, -1). Masked lanes keep v6 in v10..v35 (words 149..174).
Check() asserts Checked = 58 columns (v10..v67); v68/v69 are zeroed padding (stored, not asserted). Split into 4 adapters: 0-15, 16-31, 32-47, 48-57.
verified: disassembly (llvm-mc gfx1030): prologue v1/v3 + buffer_load_dwordx4 v[4:7] offen; [5,318) = base setup, 32-plane ds_write_b32 fill, masked sub-dword/read2/st64/b64/b96 reads into v10..v35, masked sub-dword/write2/st64/b64/b96 writes, 32 ds_read_b32 into v36..v67, v68 = v69 = 0; stores v[10:69] at offsets 0..239.
